intro.text:
MALIBU, CALIFORNIA

Tuesday evening
8:00 PM
A squawk like a fire alarm tears through the Vale mansion. Every head in the house turns toward the birdcage.
Rudebeak, darling, PLEASE. Mommy is mid-affirmation.

Evening treats, my handsome boy. Who wants a- 
Rudebeak?
The cage door hangs open. The latch is wrenched clean off. The perch is bare.
Nobody leaves. NOBODY. As of right now, this house is locked down.

8:42 PM

Outside the gates

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: Good evening. I'm Gloria Gale, live outside the Vale estate, where Hollywood's rudest bird has vanished from inside a locked house.

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: Rudebeak the macaw: star of three films, one documentary, and a talk-show incident we still cannot air. Witnesses say he was last heard squawking at eight o'clock sharp.

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: Police have sealed the house until sunrise. At dawn the gates reopen and the film trucks roll out - and whatever is hidden in that house could roll out with them.

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: So who is locked inside tonight? Let's take a look.

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: The lady of the house. Rudebeak was her co-star - and lately, sources say, the one stealing her scenes.

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: Her husband, Derek, who has not been seen downstairs all evening. He is not, we are told, a bird person.

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: Her manager, Chip Sterling, who has called this station four times tonight to say 'no comment.'

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: Petra, the bird handler. She sets out Rudebeak's supper at the same time every single evening.

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: Rosa, who runs the kitchen - and carries a key to every door in the house.

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: Basil, the gardener. Gentle, quiet, and famously opinionated about cages.

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: Director Wexler, in town shooting a documentary about the star. His whole crew is stuck in there too - grips, camera, lights and sound - with more carts and road cases than a moving company.

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: And Coco, a dinner guest who has not put her phone down since she arrived.

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: Keeping order: Officer Reyes, overheard calling this case 'a poultry matter.'

intro.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
intro.text: Somewhere in that house is a frightened bird - and somebody who knows exactly where he is. Back to you in the studio.

Under the news van, something with whiskers has been listening.
Dikkie finishes his sardine, stretches twice, and slips through the bars of the gate.
Oh, come ON. Who let a cat in? This is a crime scene, whiskers.
...Fine. You want in? Bird's gone, the doors are sealed, and somebody in there is lying to me.

Find out who took him, how he got out of a locked cage, and where he is now.
Before sunrise.

11:48 PM

The living room
The dinner gong in the hall rings. And rings. And rings. Something small and furry is hanging off the mallet.
OKAY. OKAY! The cat wants everybody in the living room. Don't ask me why I am taking orders from a cat.
One by one they file in: the star, the husband, the manager, the staff, the crew. Dikkie climbs into the empty cage, sits down, and waits for silence.
Fine. Cat. You have been sniffing around all night. Show me what you've got.
Don't look at ME. I am the victim here! Do you know what tonight is doing to her brand?
He has been panicking about headlines all night. So, cat - is panic a motive?
Dikkie swats Chip's phone off the side table. The screen lights up: a contract, fifteen percent, and a bird-shaped signature.
Fifteen percent. Of a BIRD. Who I would never, ever lose. Thank you, cat.
Manager's clean. Greedy, but clean. Next.
And before ANYONE asks: 'BETTER WITHOUT HIM' was about the reaction SHOT. Not the bird. Never the bird. Probably never the bird.
The director wanted drama and got it. Tasteless, but clean. Next.

steps.title: The Squawk at Eight

intro.text: Don't bother. I heard that bird at eight o'clock. Through noise-canceling headphones. He was ALIVE at eight.
Mid-affirmation, darling. I will never forget it. Neither will my therapist.
Two witnesses, same squawk, same minute. Whatever happened, it happened after eight. Right, cat?

steps.sentence: Derek heard the squawk at eight through the [headphones] he bought because of that bird. But Rudebeak's [supper] sat untouched since [six], and the squawk came from a speaker fed by the [line] from the sound desk - the same desk where somebody's [monitoring gear] was plugged into nothing.

success.text: Dikkie bats the little speaker out from behind the couch. It skids across the floor and stops at Derek's feet with a plastic clack.
I bought eight-hundred-dollar headphones because of that bird. And I got fooled by a SPEAKER?
So the bird was gone before six, and everything after that was a recording. Which makes every eight o'clock alibi in this room worth exactly nothing.
Derek. Darling. You did write 'him or me.' On my good stationery.
I wanted him moved to the guest house, Viv. Not STOLEN. I am a lot of things. I am not organized enough to be a thief.
And the documentary camera, darling? Pointed at my chaise all day. The cage was just out of frame. Of course it was.

steps.title: The Dinner Cart

intro.text: Which brings us to the maid. Keys to every room, a cart in the bedroom wing at seven, and feathers in her kitchen bin.
CHICKEN feathers. From the CHICKEN. I am a cook, officer, not a kidnapper.

steps.sentence: Derek counted two rumbles downstairs. One was [the first] at [seven] - the kitchen only ran one. The other was [the second] on the wing's delivery list that same minute, and Rosa's nose caught [something] in that wing that was not soup.

success.text: Dikkie walks a slow circle around Rosa's ankles, sniffs, and sneezes. Soup. Only soup.
One cart out, one cart back. Whatever else rolled through that hallway, it did not smell like my cooking.
Maid's clear. Somebody else had wheels tonight. Heavy ones.
Rosa... I may have blamed the bird's vocabulary on you.
You may have, senora. We will discuss it over paella. Which you will finally eat.

steps.title: The Broken Latch

intro.text: Then it's the gardener. In from the garden just before six, bent shears, a glove under the cage, and a whole speech about cages being prisons.
Alright! YES! I broke the latch. Me, with my shears, just before six. I wanted him free!
Well. That's a confession. Case closed, everybody. Let's all go home and-
Dikkie does not move from the cage. His tail flicks once, twice. The tail says: not yet.

steps.sentence: The kitchen logged [an errand] in from the garden, timed at [WHEN] - just before the bird's supper went untouched. The gardener's [tool] fits the wrenched latch. And at [WHEN] Coco's photo catches [a detail] at its very edge, behind the shed, watching somebody else roll past.
steps.wrongLine: Basil: 'I already SAID it was me...'

success.text: Dikkie hops onto the side table and plants a paw on Coco's phone. The 6:47 photo glows up at the room. At the very edge: a straw hat.
That's my photo! Oh my gosh. I'm a witness. I am SO a witness.
Rudebeak let himself out. He went straight to his bird bath. Then one of the crew came wheeling big black boxes up the path, and I hid behind the shed and said nothing.
I am a coward, cat. But I am not a thief.
Then who was pushing the boxes?

steps.title: The Long Evening

intro.text: Every head in the room turns toward the crew. In the corner, the Sound Guy is coiling a cable that is already coiled.
Don't look at me. I was in the LIBRARY at seven. Audio setup. It's on the schedule! Everybody check the schedule!
Marsh? Marsh is my rock. He hasn't complained about that bird in two weeks.

steps.sentence: In the book by the front door, [signature] opens the crew column at [WHEN], though the crew wasn't called until seven. At [WHEN] Coco's photo caught him rolling cases through the garden - and at [WHEN] those same cases went past the bedrooms on the wing's delivery list, signed with [scrawl].
steps.wrongLine: The Sound Guy: 'See? It doesn't add up!'

success.text: Dikkie drags three papers into a row on the rug: the guest registry, the delivery manifest, the sound desk's session log. Three signatures. Three long looping tails.
Those are just NUMBERS! Lots of people have cases! It's a film shoot, there are cases EVERYWHERE!
He's sweating, cat. Finish it.

steps.title: The Sound Guy

intro.text: You can't prove anything. You're a CAT. I don't even know why I'm still talking.

steps.sentence: The [initials] on the mixing desk's log carry the same tail: [WHO], with a grudge called the [WHY]. Before the lockdown Coco watched the cases make a [return trip] to the shed, tagged for the truck - and Rudebeak spent the evening in the dark, padded silence of the [WHAT].
steps.wrongLine: The Sound Guy: 'Ha! Wrong! ...I mean, obviously wrong.'

success.text: Dikkie leaps out of the cage, lands squarely in the Sound Guy's lap, and stares into his soul. Nobody has ever out-waited a cat.
They're EMPTY! The cases are empty, I already told you, both of them, why does nobody ever LISTEN to the sound guy-

But Dikkie is already gone: out the patio door, across the wet lawn, to the tarp behind the potting shed - the same two cases he pressed an ear to hours ago. This time he has brought people with thumbs.
Alright, cat. Let's see your empty case.
The crew tag still dangles from the latch: SPARE FOAM - RETURN TO TRUCK. Reyes reads it twice, and pops the latches anyway.
The heavy latches snap. The foam-lined lid creaks open.
Curled in the foam: Rudebeak. Perfectly dry, perfectly furious, and perfectly fine.
FORTY-SEVEN TAKES! BRAWK! FORTY-SEVEN!
Oh, you awful, wonderful bird. Somewhere dark and padded - of course he went quiet as a stone.
Forty-seven takes. You ever listen to forty-seven takes of one word while a bird screams through every single one?
In there, he was quiet. For the first time all shoot, it was QUIET. I was going to roll him out with the trucks at sunrise. Let him go somewhere nice. Somewhere far.
D. Marsh, you're coming with me. Bring your headphones. The plugged-in kind.

ending.speaker: Gloria Gale, KMAL News
ending.text: Breaking news at sunrise: Rudebeak the macaw is home, safe, and - we are told - extremely rude about it.
Solid police work, plain and simple. We followed the evidence - the registry, the photo, the speaker, the feather in the hedge, the cases. Textbook. No further questions.
On the way to the squad car, Reyes stops by the garden wall. Looks left. Looks right. Then looks down.
You're all right, cat. You're all right.
Dikkie blinks, slowly. From a cat, that is a medal.
Basil installed a brand-new latch on the cage that morning. He made it the nicest latch in Malibu - and he left it unlocked on Sundays, for the bird bath.
Rudebeak has opinions about everything that happened. He shares them hourly.

CASE CLOSED

The Missing Macaw

Dikkie will return.
